newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TENNIS-RIOS BREEZES PAST VOINEA DESPITE LEG PROBLEM.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-RIOS BREEZES PAST VOINEA DESPITE LEG PROBLEM.

text.p: Second seed Marcelo Rios, getting over a leg injury, trounced Romanian Adrian Voinea 6-1 6-4 in the first round of the European Community tennis championship on Wednesday.
World number six Rios was forced to withdraw in the second set of his final against Sweden's Thomas Enqvist in Marseille last Sunday because of a strained quadriceps muscle.
But the Chilean was declared fit to play here after treatment by a physiotherapist and produced near flawless tennis in the first set of a match which featured some breath-taking rallies.
Rios fell 2-0 behind early in the second set but quickly fought back to take the match in just over one hour.
Rios was promoted to leading player in Antwerp after Croatia's Goran Ivanisevic, the top seed, pulled out of the tournament late on Tuesday with tendinitis in his shoulder.
The organisers were worried the Chilean would also be unable to play and were relieved he came through his first match so well.
The Antwerp event, which offers a diamond-studded golden trophy to any player who wins the title three times in five years, has been hit hard by illness and injury.

Russia's Yevgeny Kafelnikov and Australian Open finalist Carlos Moya of Spain pulled out earlier this month and Ivanisevic's wihdrawal followed that of German Boris Becker, who has tendinitis in his wrist.
